$schema_note: LUMI platform registry. The single source of platform facts: install paths, capability tiers and entry files. scripts/check/check_repo.py guards it and scripts/build/build_entrypoints.py generates every per-platform artifact from it. Adding a platform means adding a record here and an install note, never restating a rule. Repository language: English only (red line). This file carries no version stamp on purpose: it is not a copy of the rules, so it has nothing to drift from, and the stamp it used to carry was hand-written, unguarded and four releases stale.

full.means: reads the bundled files and can execute scripts/
full.verification: the agent runs check_prose.py, check_design.py and inspect_layout.py itself

files.means: reads the bundled files, cannot execute anything
files.verification: the agent names the checks it owes and the operator runs them; the agent may not call a deliverable verified (references/operating-rules.md OR-9)
files.population_note: NO PLATFORM SITS HERE, and the tier is kept anyway. It is not aspirational: it describes a real shape — an agent that receives the rules, the tokens and the assets and cannot execute a script — and it is the shape of an IDE assistant reading an instructions file. The tier turned out to be empty for a different reason than it looked: `capability` was the ONE registry claim with no verification field, so ten records asserted `full` and nothing had ever confirmed it for any of them. Every record now carries capability_verified, and only claude-code is true. Some of the ten may prove to be `files` in some of their modes — a chat pane that reads a rules file but cannot run a terminal is exactly this tier. Populating it means exercising an agent and recording the result; reclassifying one from a reading of its documentation does not count.

prompt.means: one pasted prompt, no file access and no tools
prompt.verification: none available in session; the pre-delivery checklist is inlined in the prompt and the operator runs the scripts afterwards

shared_path_note: ~/.agents/skills/ is the convergent cross-agent location: Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Pi all read it, and Gemini CLI gives it precedence over its own ~/.gemini/skills/. Installing there once serves five platforms. Google Antigravity's workspace path is .agent/skills/ — singular 'agent' — and is NOT the same convention; do not conflate them.
entry_note: Every platform below reads SKILL.md, which is the Agent Skills standard artifact, except Codex which reads AGENTS.md by its own convention and the two prompt-tier platforms which take prompts/lumi-style-core.md. Per-platform pointer files (GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .cursor/rules/lumi-style.mdc) are generated conveniences, not requirements: the skill path already works without them.

platforms.name: Claude Code
drive: Bash(python3 *) Bash(cd *) Bash(sed *) Bash(grep *) Bash(ls *) Edit Write Read Glob Grep
extra: Driven with `acceptEdits` PLUS an explicit `--allowedTools` allowlist, never `bypassPermissions`. The `full` tier's claim is that the agent runs check_prose, check_design and inspect_layout itself, and acceptEdits alone permits writing files and not running commands: asked to check its own work, Claude Code stopped after 141s having written nothing and requested a `python3` allowlist entry — a tier claim the driver's own flags made impossible to meet (measured 2026-08-21). `bypassPermissions` would also have fixed it and grants arbitrary shell to an agent, on every machine that runs this harness; the allowlist grants the commands the task actually needs. WIDENED at 0.1.556: `python3` alone denied `cd <dir> && python3 …`, `sed` and `grep`, and a driven round spent 113 seconds — 9.5% of its wall clock — being refused and rephrasing. A permission the harness withholds is not a finding about the skill.

platforms.name: Gemini CLI
platforms.invoke: say "in LUMI style…"; Gemini calls activate_skill and asks you to confirm the directory
extra: `~/.agents/skills/` is the shared cross-agent location and **takes precedence** over Gemini's own directory, so prefer it — one install there also serves GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Pi.
Gemini calls `activate_skill` and asks you to confirm the directory it is about to read; approve it once per session.

Headless runs need `--skip-trust` (or `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true`). Without it the CLI prints `Approval mode overridden to "default" because the current folder is not trusted`, exits 55 in about a second, and never reaches the model — which reads as an agent failure and is not one.
platforms.capability_waiver: Not verified as a CAPABILITY claim: the CLI is installed on the maintenance machine and `run_conformance.py run --drive` drives it since 0.1.540 (conformance/CONFORMANCE.md's `cli` column carries the version it answered, read from the probe rather than written here), but `full` claims the agent runs check_prose.py, check_design.py and inspect_layout.py itself on a real deliverable through the entry file, and no run has watched it do that — its board rows come from synthetic conformance tasks. See conformance/CONFORMANCE.md.

platforms.name: Cursor
extra: A `.cursor/rules/lumi-style.mdc` pointer file ships for projects that want the rules loaded workspace-wide rather than on demand. It is a convenience — the skill path already works.

Grok 4.6 tops out at `xhigh`, not `max` — `cursor-grok-4.6-max` does not exist, and `max` in this CLI belongs to other families. Every id also has a `-fast` twin. Since 0.1.554 `--effort` without `--model` is a hard error rather than a silent 'not pinned': the composition needs both halves and a round that thought it had pinned one had pinned neither. Effort is a first-class choice in Cursor — the UI shows it beside Model — but the CLI spells it as part of the MODEL ID: `cursor-agent --list-models` returns `cursor-grok-4.6-low`, `-medium`, `-high` and `-xhigh` as separate ids. `drive_effort_in_model` composes the two so a run pins and records both axes; `--model cursor-grok-4.6` alone leaves the level to the server's default. Measured 2026-08-21: the three suffixed ids each answer exit 0, and the bracket form the CLI's own help documents (`'model[effort=low]'`) is REJECTED for them — `Cannot use this model` — because that spelling belongs to parameterized models such as `claude-opus-4-8`, not to ids that already carry the level.

`--output-format json` is declared as the usage flag rather than baked into `drive`, so one setting decides the transcript's shape and whether the run records tokens. Cursor reports them as `inputTokens`/`outputTokens` — the same shape as Claude Code's with a different spelling, which read as no usage at all until 0.1.543.
platforms.capability_waiver: Not verified as a CAPABILITY claim: run_conformance.py `run --drive` drives this agent (since 0.1.454) and its 0.1.522 T1-deck run scored every verdict ok, but a conformance task is a synthetic 12-page deck, and `full` claims the agent can run the checkers on a real deliverable through the entry file — which no run has watched. See conformance/CONFORMANCE.md.

platforms.name: Hermes
platforms.invoke: say "in LUMI style…"; `hermes skills list` shows whether it loaded, and `--skills lumi-style` preloads it for one run
platforms.docs_waiver: Hermes ships no documentation this package can cite for skill discovery. What is claimed here was MEASURED on an install instead (0.1.542) — `hermes skills list`, `hermes skills --help` and the CLI's own errors — which is a weaker source than a document and a much stronger one than the guess it replaces.
extra: Hermes files skills by CATEGORY: `~/.hermes/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md`. The category is the installer's choice and nothing depends on it — `creative` is what this package was installed under on the machine that verified this record. `hermes skills list` reports the category it actually loaded.

`--skills` resolves NAMES and installed paths, never arbitrary ones: `--skills lumi-style` and `--skills ~/.hermes/skills/creative/lumi-style` both load it, and `--skills <the repository itself>` exits 1 with `Unknown skill(s)`. Install it (a symlink into the category folder is enough) rather than pointing the flag at a checkout.

`--usage-file <path>` writes the API's own token counts as JSON — `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, cache and reasoning counts, an estimated cost and the model — to a FILE rather than the transcript, so `run --drive` reads it through `drive_usage_file_flag` instead of parsing stdout. Before 0.1.543 its runs carried quality with no cost: a clean eight-page deck and no row on the efficiency board.

`--model` names a model THIS INSTALL'S PROVIDER SERVES, not a model in general. Hermes reads its provider from `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (`deepseek`, base_url api.deepseek.com) and its key from `~/.hermes/.env`; pinned to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` on 2026-08-22 it exited 1 in 6.0s with "No usable credentials found for provider 'gmi'". The driver recorded `driver failed` with that sentence, which is the point — a pin the CLI cannot honour is a failed run and not a quiet fallback to the default. `--reasoning` takes none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max or ultra; this harness offers the five levels every driven CLI shares.
platforms.capability_waiver: Not verified as a CAPABILITY claim: the CLI is installed on the maintenance machine, `run_conformance.py run --drive` drives it since 0.1.542, and it demonstrably reads the skill's own files from a working directory outside the checkout — asked for the light palette's `--acc` value it answered #48633E, which is what `tokens/lumi-theme.css` ships. What `full` additionally claims is that the agent runs check_prose.py, check_design.py and inspect_layout.py itself on a real deliverable, and no run has watched it do that. See conformance/CONFORMANCE.md.

unlisted_note: Every other agent implementing the Agent Skills standard loads this skill from the shared ~/.agents/skills/ path with no per-platform work here: Kiro, Trae, Roo Code, Goose, Amp, Factory, Mistral Vibe, VS Code, Junie, Letta, Windsurf and others. They are not listed because this registry records only what has been checked, and an unlisted platform is not a platform we claim.
